scope: 16 selected storytelling intervals and one ambient-motion control across all eight supplied reference videos, with four words-off examples and four consecutive-frame intervals. Five official studio production/case-study pages and four official stills were inspected. This is not a new full-episode YouTube review.

cases.title: Preparation makes the takeoff understandable
cases.before: The actor is grounded over a shadow, with bent knees and raised wings.
cases.action: Knees extend and the wing stroke changes; feet separate from the ground shadow.
cases.after: The actor is visibly airborne, with the legs and wings continuing different phases of movement.
cases.visible_without_words: A winged character prepares and takes off; the movement takes effort rather than being a rigid upward slide.
cases.needs_language: Which anatomical changes could make human flight possible, and the conditional scientific argument surrounding this imagined character.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A floating final pose would omit the push, effort and change of contact that explain how the actor left the ground.
cases.lesson: Stage a readable intention, physical action and changed relationship to the environment. Keep a ground/contact reference.

cases.title: A moving particle reaches a specific attachment site
cases.before: Particle groups are separated from a row of branching receptor shapes.
cases.action: Orange particles leave the upper structure, cross the gap and settle at particular receptor tips; turquoise particles continue approaching.
cases.after: Some receptor tips retain attached particles instead of every particle merely drifting past.
cases.visible_without_words: Small objects travel to and attach at specific sites on another structure.
cases.needs_language: The identities psilocin/serotonin, receptor activation and the neurological consequences. Attachment alone does not visibly prove an electrical or biochemical signal.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A field of colored dots beside a membrane would omit the origin, direction and binding event.
cases.lesson: Give particles a source, destination, contact rule and persistent post-contact state.

cases.title: A comparison makes selective removal legible
cases.before: Two parallel connections occupy a stable view; the upper one carries repeated bright signal marks.
cases.action: Scissors enter and close across the lower connection.
cases.after: Its ends retract into a visible gap while the upper connection remains continuous.
cases.visible_without_words: One connection is deliberately severed while its neighbor is preserved.
cases.needs_language: That these represent synapses, which activity-dependent biological processes select them, and why literal scissors are a metaphor.
cases.removing_motion_loses: Two final lines, one broken, would not explain the intervention or its order. Removing the intact upper comparison would weaken the selectivity.
cases.lesson: Hold one reference unchanged while the explanatory variable changes. Preserve the resulting gap.

cases.title: Acting makes struggling with balance visible
cases.before: The baby is upright with a small footprint and arms spread for balance.
cases.action: The body leans, the limbs counterbalance, and an internal stylized view briefly emphasizes the body/brain relationship.
cases.after: The baby ends seated on the ground, with a changed facial expression.
cases.visible_without_words: The child attempts to balance or move and loses balance.
cases.needs_language: That this illustrates learning and a mental challenge. This selected range does not show a successful retry or prove improvement.
cases.removing_motion_loses: An isolated sitting baby would not communicate the failed attempt that led to the seated pose.
cases.lesson: Use whole-body poses and balance changes to communicate an attempt and outcome. Show a later successful attempt if the intended proposition is learning.

cases.title: Delivery followed by reaction gives the prop a purpose
cases.before: A bowl is positioned above an anatomical head with an alert-looking brain character.
cases.action: The bowl tilts and specks fall toward the brain.
cases.after: The brain's expression becomes drowsy and conventional sleep marks appear.
cases.visible_without_words: Something delivered from the bowl is associated with a sleepy reaction. The sleep marks contribute an established visual convention.
cases.needs_language: The substance, its chemical constituent, dose and medical interpretation. The cartoon is not a complete mechanism or dosing instruction.
cases.removing_motion_loses: Floating a bowl beside a head would not establish delivery or a change in the recipient.
cases.lesson: Connect source to recipient, then change the recipient's state. Movement should produce a consequence.

cases.title: Anatomical state change communicates danger
cases.before: The brain/head is shown with visible water-drop symbols nearby.
cases.action: Droplets depart and the anatomical head/brain silhouette contracts.
cases.after: Expressions and a red descending graphic change the scene's meaning toward harm.
cases.visible_without_words: Loss of fluid is associated with a worsening bodily state.
cases.needs_language: The prior salt exposure, osmotic mechanism, exact anatomical changes and clinical consequences. Screen-space shrinking alone is not a measurement of biological tissue loss.
cases.removing_motion_loses: An intact head with decorative droplets would not communicate loss and deterioration.
cases.lesson: Make the changed quantity and consequence visible against stable references; use color escalation after the physical change is established.

cases.title: Changing the boundary changes the experience
cases.function: Visual metaphor for a hidden process
cases.before: A small brain remains inside a circular boundary.
cases.action: The boundary shrinks/disappears; the brain remains and a colored field grows outward.
cases.after: The environment is filled by changing bands around the same brain.
cases.visible_without_words: A contained subject becomes exposed to, or surrounded by, a much larger changing field.
cases.needs_language: The specific perceptual-filter claim and its limits. This is an explanatory metaphor, not literal colored anatomy.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A psychedelic background alone would communicate mood without the prior containment and its removal.
cases.lesson: Give a metaphor a rule, show that rule changing, then let the changed rule affect the scene.

cases.title: The environment introduces a threat to ordinary work
cases.before: Farmers work recognizable rows in a cultivated field.
cases.action: A large red skull-warning sign enters the foreground and takes visual priority.
cases.after: A small land parcel/ground diagram replaces the field to introduce the next explanation.
cases.visible_without_words: An ordinary activity takes place in a dangerous setting. The warning icon supplies a familiar threat cue.
cases.needs_language: The exact hidden hazard and economic costs. This range does not visibly show the farmers stopping or a mine detonating.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A warning already present from the first frame would weaken the reveal of danger; the red foreground entrance changes what the viewer attends to.
cases.lesson: Establish normal activity before introducing the threat. Let foreground scale/value redirect attention for a reason.

cases.title: Matching vulnerable poses connect human consequences
cases.function: Empathy, stillness and a visual rhyme
cases.before: A soldier sits hunched with clasped hands, a distressed face and a weapon on the ground.
cases.action: A cut introduces a child crouched under a desk in a similarly protective pose; later a DNA symbol is overlaid.
cases.after: The child remains small and sheltered by the furniture, holding the vulnerable state.
cases.visible_without_words: Distress and protective behavior connect two human situations. The quiet staging makes vulnerability readable.
cases.needs_language: The statistical claims and any asserted intergenerational mechanism. A DNA symbol alone cannot establish how trauma is transmitted.
cases.removing_motion_loses: Removing purposeful pose/expression would weaken empathy. Adding constant idle bouncing would compete with the held emotional state.
cases.lesson: A deliberate hold can carry a story. Match meaningful body states across shots, and keep the scientific explanation distinct from the emotional analogy.

cases.title: Contact creates the consequence
cases.before: Two differently colored galaxy-like systems occupy separate positions.
cases.action: The lower system approaches and overlaps the upper one; the contact becomes increasingly luminous.
cases.after: A bright emission/burst representation occupies the collision location.
cases.visible_without_words: The two systems meeting is associated with a large energetic consequence.
cases.needs_language: Matter versus antimatter and the hypothetical nature of this scenario. Ordinary galaxy collisions must not be implied to annihilate this way.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A standalone burst would omit what interacted to produce the illustrated consequence.
cases.lesson: Show distinct participants before contact, time the response to the interaction, and preserve where it happened.

cases.title: A busy gag resolves into one explanation
cases.before: The researcher and a smaller bird share a room with many papers; the smaller bird has fallen from its perch.
cases.action: Papers move through the foreground and obscure the actors; one page separates and stays bright as the room recedes.
cases.after: A single model page becomes the next focal subject.
cases.visible_without_words: A chaotic interruption is followed by attention narrowing to one document.
cases.needs_language: What the scientific problem is and what the selected page's model asserts. The gag is not itself a physics mechanism.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A wall of equally prominent paper images would provide neither the interruption nor the selection that guides attention.
cases.lesson: Resolve visual busyness into one relevant object. Use humor to support attention and tone, with a readable return to the explanation.

cases.title: An increasing pile makes quantity tangible
cases.before: A plate receives food, forming a smaller burger grouping.
cases.action: Additional burgers drop into the same plate/stack.
cases.after: A larger food pile remains, emphasized by a radial graphic.
cases.visible_without_words: More food is required/being accumulated than in the earlier state; the plate is a stable comparison anchor.
cases.needs_language: Why food represents flight energy, the comparison with running, time interval and calorie equivalences. A growing pile alone does not specify those units.
cases.removing_motion_loses: One final food illustration would omit the smaller baseline and the act of adding more.
cases.lesson: Show quantity changing on the same anchor instead of replacing one large number with another.

cases.title: Manipulation changes the material before the analogy
cases.function: Mechanical action followed by an abstract consequence
cases.before: Hands hold the ends of several long molecular-strand illustrations.
cases.action: The strands bow and slide relative to one another as their ends are manipulated.
cases.after: A fiber with differentiated sides/charge labels and an electrical mark leads into a battery analogy.
cases.visible_without_words: Mechanical manipulation deforms an organized material, and an electrical association follows.
cases.needs_language: Collagen, piezoelectricity, charge separation and the limits of the battery analogy. The labeled signs carry essential polarity information.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A rotating finished fiber would not demonstrate the material responding to manipulation.
cases.lesson: Animate the material response to a specific force; use metaphor after the causal action, not as a replacement for it.

cases.title: A builder metaphor gives cellular work an intention
cases.before: A helmeted cell character with a bucket approaches the exposed bone surface.
cases.action: It moves to a specific surface location and brings its working hand/material toward the edge.
cases.after: Work is concentrated at that edge rather than being a decorative orbit around the diagram.
cases.visible_without_words: A builder-like agent is working on a particular surface.
cases.needs_language: Osteoblast identity, the material being deposited and the signal that recruits this work. An earlier speech bubble explicitly says the signal may involve fluid flow or electrical charge; the mechanism must not be presented as settled.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A helmeted cell floating beside bone would retain the costume but omit the destination and work.
cases.lesson: Design the character's action around its job. Preserve explicit uncertainty instead of making a smooth animation imply a solved mechanism.

cases.title: An orbit accumulates a visible consequence
cases.before: An orbiting body travels around Earth with relatively little visible ring material.
cases.action: Tracks/material accumulate around the same orbit as the body continues moving.
cases.after: A ring becomes visible, changes/fades, and the orbital subject persists.
cases.visible_without_words: Repeated travel is associated with an accumulating ring and its later change.
cases.needs_language: Io, sulfur, the proposed scenario, ring persistence and physical mechanism. The source's not-to-scale note is important and remains visible.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A rotating moon beside an already finished ring would omit accumulation and change over time.
cases.lesson: Let an object's action leave an explanatory trace in the environment, with an initial state and persistent result.

cases.title: An expectation hold prepares an environmental payoff
cases.before: Observers sit beneath a large quiet sky.
cases.action: A few colored fragments appear overhead before wider auroral curtains spread through the sky.
cases.after: The sky has become the main event while the observers give it a human scale and point of view.
cases.visible_without_words: People are watching a striking sky event develop.
cases.needs_language: How particles from the hypothetical moon scenario would produce it. A beautiful aurora does not independently explain the preceding magnetic interaction.
cases.removing_motion_loses: A fully lit sky from the outset would omit expectation, arrival and reveal.
cases.lesson: Reserve a quiet state so an environmental change can become an event. Keep the observer's attention aligned with it.

cases.title: Control: moving water does not independently explain tides
cases.before: A stylized ocean and night sky occupy the scene.
cases.action: Water highlights move and a pier/observer enters the framing.
cases.after: The viewer has a situated ocean view, but this selected range does not stage a clear repeated high/low tide comparison.
cases.visible_without_words: A person is by an ocean with moving highlights.
cases.needs_language: The moon's density and the claim about altered tides. Those facts cannot be recovered from the ambient motion in this range alone.
cases.removing_motion_loses: Removing the highlights reduces atmosphere but does not remove a visually demonstrated tide mechanism, because one is not established in this interval.
cases.lesson: Atmosphere has a legitimate role, but it cannot substitute for the event or comparison that must teach the intended idea.

uncertainty_context.note: The original speech bubble explicitly preserves uncertainty about the recruitment signal; it is retained as evidence of what language must clarify.

method_limits: Analyst knows the topics and has inspected original frames; this is not a blind study or audience experiment.
Caption masks obscure all pixels in their rectangles, including some actors/props. Original files remain unchanged.
Only four words-off cases remove additional readable labels; scientific labels/icons remain in the others.
GIFs are silent, scaled to 240px and 20fps, with artificial restarts. Dense sheets retain 24 consecutive decoded source-frame records.
Before/action/after strips are analyst-selected states; a juxtaposition is not automatically proof of a scientific mechanism.
Motion inference applies to the uploaded clips; official stills/text support only composition or stated production intentions.
No new production animation, narration or API-funded assets are generated by this study.
